checks: No eclipse at 3 of 56 covered epochs where the 0.82899 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 403017570 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.8290 days, where the primary eclipse produces a 0.43% dimming of the star's light. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected this signal with a high detection significance of 1074.8 using the Box Least Squares algorithm, and pixel-level image analysis confirmed the signal's location with a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 27.0, though the centroid offset of 9.7 arcseconds from the target warrants consideration. No secondary eclipse was detected in the available data. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel finding, and the machine-learning screening model assigned it a score of 0.96, indicating strong consistency with expected characteristics of a real eclipsing binary system.
